images.title: Halving past one unit
images.purpose: Shows the halving of 16 continued past 1 unit to half a unit, which is written as 2 with exponent −1.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. Six horizontal bars stacked one under another from one left edge, each half as long as the one above, with only the last two coloured.
images.exact_structure: Six horizontal bars, left ends aligned. Lengths in units, top to bottom: 16, 8, 4, 2, 1, 1/2, drawn to scale. The first four bars are plain light grey (#6B7280). Bar 5 (length 1) is teal (#0072B2). Bar 6 (length 1/2) is reddish purple (#CC79A7) and has a thick outline. To the right of each bar, in order, the labels '2⁴', '2³', '2²', '2¹', '2⁰', '2⁻¹'; in '2⁻¹' the raised minus is a true minus sign, not a hyphen. The label '16' at the right end of bar 1 under its power, and the label '1/2' beside bar 6. Exactly 6 bars.

images.takeaway: Halving past 1 gives fractions: 2 to the power −1 is 1/2.
images.description: Shows the halving of 16 continued past 1 unit to half a unit, which is written as 2 with exponent −1.
images.context: 16 halved 5 times is 16 ÷ 32 = 1/2, so 2⁴ ÷ 2 to the power 5 is 2 to the power −1. Halved 10 times: 16 ÷ 1024 = 1/64, which is 2 to the power −6.
images.teaching_notes: Grey bars repeat the earlier halving; colour marks only the step to 1 and the step past it.

image_decisions.why: Continuing the halving past 1 is where negative exponents come from, which is this concept.
